subject: Basketry
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are taken at one sitting. Paper 1: forty multiple-choice questions in 50 minutes for 40 marks. Paper 2: six essay-type questions, answer four, in 2 hours for 60 marks. Paper 3: two practical projects of which one is executed in five days at six hours per day for 80 marks; question papers are sent two weeks earlier and sketches and preparatory notes done in that period carry 20 marks, making 100 marks.
excluded: The Ghanaian colour concept and symbolism item under Elements of Design (Ghana-specific).

topics.name: Meaning and Scope of Basketry
objectives: Identify the areas covered in basketry: coiled work, woven articles, frame works, macrame etc.
Make articles such as baskets, hats, mats, nets, couch, footwear, cot etc.
Describe the characteristics of materials and tools
Design and make articles using techniques of weaving, plaiting, coiling, stitching, knotting and construction
Combine basketry with other materials such as cowries, gourd, beads etc. to produce rattle, macrame etc.

topics.name: Rationale for Studying Basketry
objectives: Make creative use of new materials for articles of cultural, functional and aesthetic value
Acquire skills for employment and further studies
Explain the role of basketry in tourism promotion

topics.name: History, Social, Cultural and Economic Importance
objectives: Describe the origin of basketry
Describe the social use of basketry, e.g. entertainment
Explain the cultural importance of basketry
Explain the economic importance of basketry in society, e.g. in agriculture and commerce

topics.name: Places, People and Basketry
objectives: Describe the contribution of people and places to basketry

topics.name: Competencies and Attitudes
objectives: Acquire knowledge, creative thinking, skills and values for employment, e.g. weaving and designing
Show tolerance, diligence, honesty and commitment
Develop communication skills and time-management

topics.name: Types and Characteristics of Materials
objectives: Identify materials: natural, synthetic, flexible/pliable, stiff/rigid etc.

topics.name: Preparation of Materials
objectives: Apply skills and techniques for preparation, e.g. drying and wetting
Store and care for materials (chemical and non-chemical methods)
Preserve sources of materials, e.g. ecology and bush burning
Discover characteristics of materials and their uses in the making of articles

topics.name: Tools and Their Uses
objectives: Categorise, describe and state the uses of tools
Draw and label tools
Improvise tools
Care for and maintain tools and observe safety precautions

subtopics.name: Elements of design
objectives: Identify the elements of design in the environment, e.g. dot, line, shape
Create the elements using appropriate techniques of knotting, weaving etc., e.g. bead or knot for a dot and waling for texture
Use the 12-point colour wheel

subtopics.name: Principles of design
objectives: Identify the principles of design in the environment, e.g. unity, balance, proportion, repetition
Create the principles of design using appropriate techniques, e.g. spraying, scorching, weaving

topics.name: Basic Design and Technology
objectives: Define design
Create ideas and design by drawing from memory, imagination and observation
Use appropriate techniques, tools and materials

topics.name: Designing Articles to Suit Specific Needs
objectives: Design an article by hand or computer
Make articles to satisfy specific needs using techniques in weaving, knotting, plaiting, coiling, stitching, framing etc.
Apply criteria for appreciation and evaluation, e.g. appropriate material, colour, technique, finishing

topics.name: Sustainable Development of Basketry
objectives: Explore strategies of sustaining sources of raw materials, e.g. re-afforestation and waste management
Identify and seek solutions to problems of the industry, e.g. competition with plastic products and material acquisition
Apply solutions such as formation of co-operatives and remaining competitive

topics.name: Decoration and Finishing
objectives: Define decoration and finishing
Describe processes of decoration, e.g. use of coloured and uncoloured weavers, weave variations, scorching, spraying and use of complementary objects
Describe processes of finishing, e.g. wrapping, binding, singeing, tying, trimming, lashing, bending, gluing, sanding, varnishing, lacquering, embroidering, sealing, borders

topics.name: Entrepreneurial Skills in Practice
topics.content: Portfolio, e.g. prints, photos, CDs, DVDs. Business plan: meaning, purpose, steps towards business organization such as registration, capital, location of set-up, materials and tools, market survey. The business: capital (e.g. bank loan, co-operatives); exhibition (general, specialized); business promotion (billboard, internet, print media, TV, radio, handbills, posters). Packaging and handling: definition, function, disadvantages, types (primary, secondary and tertiary). Costing and pricing: variable cost, fixed cost, profit, and factors of price determination.

subtopics.name: Portfolio and business plan
objectives: Prepare a portfolio
Explain the meaning and purpose of a business plan
Describe steps towards business organization: registration, capital, location, materials and tools, market survey

subtopics.name: The business, exhibition and promotion
objectives: Identify sources of capital, e.g. bank loan and co-operatives
Distinguish types of exhibition: general and specialized
Describe business promotion through billboard, internet, print media, TV, radio, handbills and posters

subtopics.name: Packaging and handling
objectives: Define packaging and handling and state their function and disadvantages
Distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary packaging

subtopics.name: Costing and pricing
objectives: Distinguish variable cost, fixed cost and profit
State the factors of price determination
